Residualise the outcome on covariates using untreated cells only

Source: R/project_out_covariates.R
project_out_covariates.Rd

The covariate adjustment of Kranz (2022): regress the outcome on the covariates with unit and time fixed effects, using only the untreated unit-periods – every control-unit cell plus the treated unit's pre-period – then subtract the covariates' fitted contribution from the whole outcome matrix. Fitting on untreated cells keeps the treatment effect out of the covariate coefficients. The residualised matrix is then passed to fit_sdid() as Y with no X.

Usage

project_out_covariates(Y, X, N0, T0)

Arguments

Y

Outcome matrix, units x periods, controls first and the treated unit last.

X

Units x periods x covariates array aligned with Y (a units x periods matrix is accepted for a single covariate).

N0

Number of control units.

T0

Number of pre-treatment periods.

Value

Y with the covariates' estimated contribution removed, with the coefficients attached as the "beta" attribute. A covariate that is collinear with the fixed effects gets an NA coefficient and is left out of the adjustment.

Details

This is the alternative to handing X to synthdid, which estimates the coefficients jointly with the synthetic-control weights. The two can give materially different answers when the covariates are strongly related to the outcome; comparing them is a useful robustness check.

The coefficients are estimated once, on the real treatment assignment. Placebo inference on the residualised matrix therefore holds them fixed rather than re-estimating them for each placebo.

References

Kranz, S. (2022). Synthetic Difference-in-Differences with Time-Varying Covariates. Working paper.

Examples

# \donttest{
data("california_prop99", package = "synthdid")
setup <- synthdid::panel.matrices(california_prop99)
set.seed(1)
X <- setup$Y * 0.01 + rnorm(length(setup$Y))
Yres <- project_out_covariates(setup$Y, X, setup$N0, setup$T0)
attr(Yres, "beta")
#>        x1 
#> 0.7019451 
# }
